why: The answer predicts no output for any of the three inputs and treats StdIn as a variable that holds all the numbers like an array, which contradicts Java because StdIn is a library that reads from a stream and uses up each value as it reads it.

concepts.quote: StdIn is a variable that holds all the numbers
concepts.why: StdIn is a library of static methods that read the next token from the input stream, not a variable that stores the input.

concepts.quote: a variable that holds all the numbers, like an array
concepts.why: This is the MultiValueVariable misconception, because a variable holds exactly one value at a time.
The answer says nothing about the isEmpty() test, the read in the loop body, or the sum and count updates.

concepts.quote: holds all the numbers, like an array
concepts.why: It treats input as a stored list that stays in place, but a stream is used up in order as it is read and cannot be revisited.
